events.title: The opening of the Second Vatican Council
events.shortBlurb: Pope John XXIII opened the twenty-first ecumenical council before a great gathering of the world's bishops…
body: On 11 October 1962 Pope John XXIII solemnly opened the Second Vatican Council in the basilica of St. Peter, with more than two thousand bishops from around the world in attendance, the largest such gathering in the Church's history. In his opening address, Gaudet Mater Ecclesia, the pope set out his hope that the Council would present the unchanging faith in a way suited to the needs of the age.

Over four sessions, continuing under Pope Paul VI until 1965, the Council produced sixteen documents on the liturgy, the Church, revelation, and the Church's relation to the modern world. Its decisions, including the reform of the liturgy and a renewed emphasis on the universal call to holiness, profoundly shaped Catholic life in the decades that followed. The 11th of October was later chosen as the memorial of St. John XXIII, who had convoked it.

sources.text: Vatican, Documents of the Second Vatican Council (vatican.va)
